messages:
Alex C: Heads-up — after the runtime merge (abcd1234) we're seeing a 2.5-3x token/sec drop for short-ctx continuous-batcher traffic. CI perf check failed on the canary.
Priya S: ugh, any numbers? which workload/profile?
Alex C: small-ctx r/w baseline (v1.28.2): ~28k tok/s. after merge: ~9.2k tok/s. 95p latency jumped 120ms -> 480ms. median batch size fell 8 -> 2. KV cache hit-rate dropped too (see below).
Dmitri V: can you paste the CI perf link + bisect steps? i'll start a bisect locally.
Alex C: CI perf job: https://ci.reddemo/internal/Perf/786/artifacts
Alex C: quick bisect plan:
```
git checkout v1.28.2
git bisect start HEAD v1.28.2
# run minimal load test that reproduces token/sec drop
```
perf-bot: Perf regression detected on run 786: metric=token_sec delta=-67% p<0.01. Suspected range: commits abcd1000..abcd1300.
Dmitri V: bisect narrowed to abcd1234 (author: maria/l). That commit touched scheduler/batching heuristics + kv cache key normalization.
Maria L: confirmed. abcd1234: "adjust batch_window_ms to 12ms; change kv key hash to xx64 to avoid collisions" — the intent was to reduce tiny batches and fix rare key collisions, but didn't expect this regression.
Jason R: short profile (flame lines) under repro:
```
top functions by CPU:
continuous_batcher::drain_loop 42%
scheduler::select_worker 18%
kv_cache::lookup 12%
kernel_selector::score 8%
```
Jason R: also saw a lot of time in scheduler lock contention. stack traces show wakeups on new_batch path.
Priya S: KV hit-rate numbers: before: 71.8% after: 31.4% on the small-ctx traces (same traffic). that explains a lot of token re-compute and smaller batches.
Alex C: reproduced locally with loadtool:
```
workload --profile small-ctx --qps 200 --duration 5m
# watch metrics: tok/s, batch_median, kv_hitrate
```
Alex C: Observed median batch_size=2, kv_hitrate=33%, tok/s=9.4k. Reverting abcd1234 to v1.28.2 in canary brings tok/s back to ~27k within 2 mins.
Dmitri V: sounds like two regressions coupled: batch_window bump increased early flushes for certain sequences AND kv hash change reduced cache reuse. either alone might have been OK, together they're devastating.
Maria L: agreed. immediate plan: revert the merge on canary, open a follow-up that splits the changes. I'll own the follow-up (restore old hash + add compatibility flag, revert batch window change and add adaptive heuristic).
Alex C: please also add a perf check to the PR that runs the small-ctx continuous-batcher scenario (fast smoke perf).
Maria L: copy — creating PR: https://git.reddemo/p/runtime/pulls/4123 (WIP) — revert on canary now blocked by in-flight traffic, asking ops to roll back.
deploy-bot: Rolling back canary to tag v1.28.2 now (initiated by @dmitri). ETA 90s.
deploy-bot: Canary rollback complete — health checks green.
Priya S: after rollback tok/s back to 26.7k, median batch_size=7, kv_hitrate=73%. good.
Jason R: long term we should add a cheap perf unit test that asserts median batch_size for small-ctx > 4 under synthetic traffic and kv_hitrate > 60% for same key distribution.
Dmitri V: agreed. action items: Maria to split & rework PR (owner), Jason to add unit perf test + CI job, Alex to run extended canary after PR, Priya to add regression alert on kv_hitrate drop. target: patch + CI by EOD, canary re-run tomorrow morning.
Maria L: noted, I'll queue the split now and ping infra for a gated canary.
Alex C: thanks everyone. once the split lands let's run a quick perf smoke before allowing the rollout. :thumbsup:
